clue.text: Shakespearian character found hanging in a dusty chamber?

definitions.meaning: one of the fairies attending Titania in A Midsummer Night's Dream

definitions.text: found hanging in a dusty chamber?
definitions.meaning: the spider's tangled web strung across the corners of a neglected room

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second sense as a whimsical description rather than a dictionary definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a fairy in Shakespeare's comedy and to the dusty spider's web of a neglected room.

clue.text: Like some boats initially, as recorded in the dictionary

indicators.note: in places the first letters inside the dictionary's abbreviation

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of as and of recorded

explanation.surface: A definition of a kind of boat, as first written up in the dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Boats propelled by oars are rowed rather than sailed.

clue.text: Health will almost break the Government here

indicators.note: break suggests smashing the letters up and reassembling them
almost cuts the final letter from will

explanation.surface: The state of the nation's health is about to bring down the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims WILL to WIL, and 'break' rearranges HEALTH plus WIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The London street of ministries stands by metonymy for the British civil service and government.

clue.text: Angel cake originally stocked by a suitable retailer

indicators.note: the letter is stocked, held inside, by the shop owner

parts.note: a baker is the right shopkeeper to sell cake

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of cake

explanation.surface: An angel cake is sold first by a fitting shop.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'angel' in theatre is a financial investor in a show; angel cake is the surface misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical investor who funds a production is its financial supporter.

clue.text: Left complete, say, it lets in light for travellers

definitions.text: it lets in light for travellers

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship

indicators.note: say signals that the word for complete is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: complete means whole

explanation.surface: A list of a ship window's virtues: it lets light in for passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns WHOLE into its sound-alike HOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's round window admits daylight to passengers' cabins.

clue.text: Reason for absence of tax form — it's too late to go back now

definitions.text: Reason for absence of tax form
definitions.meaning: a point is a reason, and no return is the absence of a tax form, so the phrase is read literally

definitions.text: it's too late to go back now
definitions.meaning: the moment past which turning back is impossible

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase literally: 'point' is a reason, and 'no return' means no tax return filed.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage after which reversing course is no longer possible.

clue.text: Bird standing outside broken-down shed

indicators.note: outside puts the word for standing around the other letters

parts.note: rank means status or standing

indicators.note: broken-down shuffles the letters of shed

explanation.surface: A bird is perched beside a dilapidated shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' means rank or status, not upright; 'broken-down' rearranges the shed into EDSH, and 'outside' wraps the rank round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wading bird with red legs, an example of a shore bird.

clue.text: Audio-visual part of bird sanctuary

indicators.note: the abbreviation becomes part of the bird, set inside it

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: Audio-visual equipment forms part of a bird reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A safe refuge or harbour is a sanctuary.

clue.text: Too apathetic to make lace? Right

indicators.note: to make asks for the letters to be worked into something new

explanation.surface: Someone too listless to do some lacework, admits it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' rearranges LACE and RIGHT; 'Right' looks like an exclamation of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggish and lacking energy, so too listless to bother.

clue.text: Lines written by a trendy kid — an original work

parts.note: BR is British Rail, whose railway lines are a crossword staple
in means fashionable
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: Verses written by a fashionable youngster prove an original creation.
explanation.walkthrough: BR stands for British Rail, the old national railway, so 'Lines' gives those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet invention or idea that someone has thought up is an original creation of their mind.

clue.text: Ban imposed in repressive totalitarian states

indicators.note: the run of letters is set inside the words repressive totalitarian, straddling the gap

explanation.surface: A prohibition is enforced in oppressive regimes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'states' is a link meaning 'says'; the letters run across the end of repressive and the start of totalitarian.
explanation.definitionFit: A prohibition or formal refusal to allow something.

clue.text: A hanger-on we may be stuck with!

definitions.text: A hanger-on we may be stuck with!

parts.words: A hanger-on we may be stuck with!
parts.note: a loyal follower is a hanger-on, and literally something that clings or sticks fast

explanation.walkthrough: The word means both a faithful supporter and, literally, something that sticks to a surface; 'stuck with' plays on the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower who clings to a cause, from a Latin verb meaning to stick to.

clue.text: Shed in which to execute a Republican

parts.note: to hang someone is to execute them

explanation.surface: A grim instruction: use the outbuilding to put a Republican to death.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft shed is a large building for housing planes.

clue.text: Home of Pistol's "hollow pamper'd jades"

parts.note: in Henry IV Part 2 the braggart Pistol rants about the hollow pampered jades of a continent, misquoting Marlowe's Tamburlaine

explanation.walkthrough: Pistol is Falstaff's swaggering companion; his line runs 'hollow pamper'd jades of' the continent named here, jades being worn-out horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent named in Pistol's quoted line is where those horses come from.

clue.text: A day one state annexed another? It's ironic

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday, a day
I is the Roman numeral for one
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
Cal is short for California, another US state

explanation.surface: One state annexing another one day; there's irony in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'annexed' only joins the pieces; RI and CAL are both US state abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking and sardonic, as satire is.

clue.text: Dance devised to rouse the tribe to action

parts.note: to fan is to stir up or rouse, as flames or passions
Dan is one of the twelve tribes of Israel
go means a turn or bout of action, as in 'have a go'

explanation.surface: A dance invented to stir the tribesmen into battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Spanish dance in triple time, performed by a couple.

clue.text: One publishing new name in race riot

indicators.note: in places the two short pieces inside the scrambled letters
riot suggests disorder, so the letters of race run wild

parts.note: a noun is a naming word

explanation.surface: Someone reports a new name in a race riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riot' gives ACER, a rearrangement of race; 'in' sets the new name inside it after the A. 'publishing' here means announcing publicly.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster who makes public statements, publishing news.

clue.text: Like gold held in firm

indicators.note: held in puts the heraldic gold inside the word for firm

parts.note: stable means steady or firm
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Gold kept safely in a business vault.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer: gold kept in a firm is the kind of thing that can be put away; 'firm' as an adjective gives STABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable of being kept in a store or vault, as bullion is.

clue.text: Good man — one permitted to display a dagger

parts.note: ST stands for saint, a good man
I is the Roman numeral for one
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A virtuous man is allowed to show off his knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A short dagger with a slender tapering blade.

clue.text: Subtle 24 misses the central point

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is E, also the compass point east, and it is dropped

parts.note: 24 is the answer to the clue at 24 down, a brother's or sister's daughter

explanation.surface: A delicate relative misses the main issue.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 24 down has E at its centre; E is also a compass point, so 'the central point' names it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine distinction is a delicate, subtle one.

clue.text: Keep two boys

parts.note: Don is a boy's name
Jon is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Hold on to the two lads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb but is the noun: the great central tower of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The strongest tower of a castle, its central keep.

clue.text: Tradesman who sounds more like Falstaff

indicators.note: sounds signals that the comparative is heard, not written

parts.note: Falstaff is famously fat, so someone more like him is grosser

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who sounds rather like Shakespeare's fat knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Falstaff is Shakespeare's enormously fat knight, so 'more like Falstaff' is GROSSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper selling food and household goods.

clue.text: Keen on exercises — they make us vault

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry in grief
PT is physical training, exercises

explanation.surface: Enthusiastic about exercises that let us leap over the horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' seems to mean eager and 'vault' a gymnastic leap; really it is to wail, and vault is an underground chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground chamber beneath a church, a burial vault.

clue.text: Persuasive party taken in to queen's assembly

indicators.note: the party's letter is taken in, placed inside the rearranged letters
assembly suggests the letters being put together in a new order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter; the rest is rearranged
L stands for Liberal, a political party

explanation.surface: A convincing political group is drawn into the monarch's gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' rearranges the letters of 'to queen' into EOQUENT, and 'taken in' slips L in after its first letter. 'Party' is not DO here but a political party, the Liberals.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluent, forceful speech that sways listeners is persuasive.

clue.text: The pawnbroker's daughter?

parts.note: a pawnbroker is slangily called uncle, so his daughter is a relation to an uncle

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a pawnbroker is 'uncle', so 'his daughter' is read as the girl an uncle is related to.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is related to her uncle in this way.

clue.text: Suffering, but always in church? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: in on its own would put the word for always inside the word for church
this reverses the container: the church letters go inside the always letters instead

parts.note: ay is an old or poetic word for always

explanation.surface: Someone forever suffering in church, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, 'always in church' would put the always-word inside the church abbreviation; 'Quite the opposite' tells you to swap which piece holds which.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling aches, as an adjective for someone in pain.

clue.text: The seaman is a Tory supporter, it's said

definitions.meaning: a sailor in the navy, so called from the uniform

explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative (Tory) party, so the second half pictures a party supporter in a blue coat; 'it's said' signals the playful naming.
explanation.definitionFit: A navy sailor, named for the blue uniform coat, and whimsically a wearer of the Conservative colour.

clue.text: Slovenly woman following another in heartless sin

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
heartless removes the middle letter of the word sin

parts.note: the latter is the second of two, the one following the other

explanation.surface: A slovenly woman comes after another in a cold-hearted sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle letter of sin to leave SN; 'following another' is the second of two, the one named last.
explanation.definitionFit: An untidy, dirty woman; a slut in the old sense.

clue.text: In retirement, manage quarters for health workers

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for manage is read backwards

parts.note: to run means to manage
S, E and S are points of the compass, the quarters

explanation.surface: Retired staff manage the living quarters of hospital workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retirement' turns RUN into NUR; the compass quarters supply S, E, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital staff who care for the sick are health workers.
